text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam hopes that new regulations, which come into effect in June, will promote exports and rein in the trade deficit. Trade Minister Le Van Triet has estimated the trade gap for this year at $4.3 billion.
-- Two agreements are due to be signed between Vietnam and Sweden on Tuesday on bilateral co-operation and strengthening Vietnam's environment management authority.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has asked the State Bank of Vietnam and the Ministry of Planning and Investment to study the possibility of setting up a joint-stock bank which would specialise in raising capital for the Mekong Delta region. The state would hold a 50-percent stake in the Mekong Delta Housing and Development Bank, whose total registered capital would be between $90 million and $135 million.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has raised 1997's rice export quota by a further one million tonnes. A previous quota for the first nine months of the year was two million tonnes.
-- The judgement board in the trial of Vietnam's biggest drug-trafficking case will go into a one-day recess on Tuesday to decide on verdicts for the 22 defendants.

-- Vietnam's biggest sugar-processing plant was put into operation in early May. A joint-venture between a Taiwanese suger cane company and a local partner from Thanh Hoa province, the plant's capacity will be 600 tonne of suger per day.
-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment, in cordination with United Nations Investment and Development Organisation, held a seminar on Monday to boost relations between enterprises and banks.
